To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the implementation of ERP system is not always a success story, 2) the implementation of the ERP system can be successful when the ERP system is implemented with the support of a strong project management team, 3) the implementation of an ERP system is not a one-time activity, and 4) the implementation of a successful ERP project requires the involvement of all stakeholders.
ERP failure occurs when the assumptions and requirements of ERP design do not match the realities of the client organization.
ERP failure occurs because the design of the software is not compatible with the actual reality of the organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role and impact of information technology in organisations.
the role that the ERP system design and the client’s business processes have in the failure or the success of an ERP implementation project.
the design of ERP systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the failure of the ERP implementation at the Jordanian company studied is due to the inability of the company to close the gaps between the design and the actual reality of the company.
the ERP failure in this Jordanian manufacturing firm was a consequence of the failure of the ERP implementation team to bridge the design‐reality gap.
the ERP failure was due to the inability of the organization to manage and control the project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design-reality gap model can be applied in developing countries, but with some caveats.
ERP implementation in developing countries is a complex process that is not well understood by the organizations and the vendors.
ERP systems are not a panacea for the problems that many developing countries face, and that they are not the only way to achieve business success.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ERP systems are not a panacea for organisational performance problems.
ERP failure is a complex and multi‐faceted phenomenon, which is not adequately explained by any single factor.
the design-reality gap is a key driver of ERP failure, and that this is particularly the case in developing country contexts.
